items.title: 68088_Wilbur B. Ware, Sr oral history interview
items.q: I played and he was learning. You know, I'd show him what I knew

ctx.x: However, this particular morning, I would come in the club, the Mocambo, a little bar, it was owned by Leonard and Phil Chess, who later had the Chess recording company -- and I used to work Monday nights there.

But anyway, I go in there and it's morning -- with and Malachi and a couple of the guys we were hanging out with, and the bandstand was kind of full -- and Flip the trumpet player, we went to school together -- he was working with Red Saunders' band at the time -- he's up jamming, and he says, "C'mon, come up on stage; come up and play" -- you know. So the bass player gave up the fiddle and I end up playing, and we had a good groove going on, and I noticed they pushed me out in front, you know? Go solo. I'm Not…

I started playing, Pettiford had been sitting up there with his head down on the table, you know, between some other musicians, and when I started playing, he raised his head up and started listening.
